why: Review of d8710f755, in next/, test code and field rows only: merge-ready, one finding row. The new law 'Q9/Q12 a refused send whose span crosses the hour charges the program's local account no write and no byte' checks its title: it turns the hour inside one refused send (a hook on the stand-in Project transport, at that send's first route call), requires that the turn happened from the old hour, checks each refusal is counted in the hour its span ended and not the other, and checks the program's local account is unchanged after each refusal and after the read that follows. A plant of mine went red: supervisor.ts's healthy handler also saving on the first idle turn in a new hour failed with 'the read after refusal 0 changed the program's local account: writes 16 against 15'; the file was restored and git status was clean. The one-second drift claim holds against the installed effect 4.1.3 (dist/internal/effect.js, wallTimeNanos re-anchors to Date.now() only when skew is over 1_000_000_000 ns; the repo's effect patch does not touch it): with Date frozen, early of at least 1100 ms keeps every span before the turn in the old hour, and early plus late of at least 2100 ms forces a re-anchor on the first read after the turn, at any machine speed. The healthy-mark guard (early plus late at most 3800 ms against resetAfterMs 5000) keeps a 1 s margin for that drift. The Date fake is acquired and released in the law's own scope, as the neighbor Q9/Q12 law does. The new beforeProject hook defaults to a no-op and only the new law sets it, so loosening.sh's one hit (line 534) loosens no law.
